Subject: Cross-border tax matrix: VAT/GST treatment for mixed-supply marketplace (platform fees + seller payouts)

Hi Soham —

Thanks for raising the mixed-supply edge cases for ClearCart. I pulled together a preliminary matrix (attached) that separates the invoice lines and shows when we should apply reverse-charge vs collect VAT or trigger APAC withholding/TCS flows. High level summary: 

- Platform fee (redwood -> ClearCart): typically a service. For EU B2B customers with a validated VAT ID we can apply reverse-charge (customer accounts for VAT) and issue a net invoice; otherwise standard VAT applies.
- Seller payouts (we invoice marketplace fee on gross seller proceeds): treatment depends on whether the underlying sale is goods or digital service and the seller's tax registration. For EU sales of goods, VAT follows place of supply rules; for digital services, look to OSS or supplier registration.
- India: marketplace operator rules vary — there may be withholding or TCS obligations depending on whether ClearCart is treated as an aggregator/marketplace operator and whether the seller is registered. We flagged this separately in the tax matrix.

I attached: tax_matrix_draft.xlsx (workbook with per-jurisdiction rules), plus a reissue_invoice_template.pdf we usually use when converting a gross invoice to a reverse-charge net invoice.

Can you confirm: 
1) Which seller line items you want us to split on the invoice (software vs hardware)?
2) Do you have the seller's VAT registration document and a VIES check screenshot for the UK/EU ID? (If VIES shows pending, we typically request a certificate copy).

I'll loop in Finance (Ben) to validate the reissue flow and Vanessa for collection implications. Proposed next step: we validate the VAT IDs, reissue the invoice (if eligible) with reverse-charge footnote, and hold on collection changes until we confirm seller documentation.

Best,

On Mon, Apr 20, 2026 at 08:22 AM Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the details, Soham. See suggestions below.

Soham — quick operational recommendations from Finance: 

1) Evidence threshold
- EU/UK reverse-charge: prefer VIES confirmation + seller-signed VAT certificate (registration PDF). If VIES shows pending, we accept a government-issued VAT registration PDF with seller name + VAT number as temporary evidence (attach to invoice file).
- If neither available, invoice should be issued VAT-inclusive and we keep a tax-hold flag until proof is provided. We can do a post-invoice credit/reissue if proof arrives within 60 days.

2) Invoice line handling (practical template)
- Generate invoice with separate lines: Platform fee (net with reverse-charge footnote when applicable), Seller goods (taxable per destination rules), Fulfillment (split by jurisdiction).
- For reverse-charge lines include this footnote: "Reverse-charge applies under Article 194 of the VAT Directive / domestic equivalent. Recipient shall account for VAT." (we'll adapt depending on jurisdiction).

3) India (APAC) fallback and collection
- For Indian marketplace-supplied goods, we recommend ClearCart work with local counsel. Operationally, if seller is non-resident/unregistered, mark the line for TCS/withholding review; do not automatically gross-up platform fee. If ClearCart is required to withhold, you'll need a separate remit flow and reporting.

4) Reissue flow
- If we need to convert a gross invoice to reverse-charge we can: issue a credit note against the gross invoice and then issue a new net invoice. Attached is the reissue_invoice_template.pdf. Finance needs signed confirmation from buyer that they accept reverse-charge bookkeeping for their VAT return.

Next steps: Mina to coordinate seller documentation collection; Vanessa to confirm whether collection timelines must change if reissue occurs; Soham — if you can request the VAT certificate from Arun and upload to your portal we can validate and move forward.
